newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia details funding for 1997 wheat sowing.
newsitem.headline: Serbia details funding for 1997 wheat sowing.

text.p: Serbia's government expects to collect 900 million dinars ($128 million) through an issue of wheat forward selling contracts to finance the 1997 wheat sowing, government officials said on Friday.
"This is a turning point in financing the autumn sowing," Garip Hadzini, assistant to the republic's finance minister told a news conference.
"It is the first time that about 1.2 million tonnes of wheat from the harvest on at least 400,000 hectares is purchased prior to sowing," he said.
About one million tonnes of the 1997 wheat crop will be financed through forward contracts at a price of 0.90 dinars per kg, Hadzini said.
Price remained the same as for the 1996 wheat crop, he said. "The financing conditions are stable now and we do not expect the price of wheat to change."
Darinka Jelovac, acting director of the Serbian Commodity Reserve Agency, said the government expected to mobilise all the available surplus liquidity for financing the wheat sowing.
"We expect strong interest from banks and companies with surplus liquidity to buy forward contracts especially because they carry the state guarantee," Jelovac said.
Hadzini said that a 32 percent discount on those securities along with other advantages would attract banks and companies. "Investors could freely sell wheat on domestic or foreign market."
He said the government would call on the central bank to allow commercial banks to use half of their 10 percent reserve requirement for purchasing wheat selling forward contracts.

Srboljub Stankovic, the republic's deputy minister for agriculture, said about 192,000 tonnes of wheat would be financed through barter arrangements, with farmers paid in kind -- in wheat seed, fertiliser and diesel.
"The government has secured about 300,000 tonnes of fertilisers and enough diesel and wheat seed for the planned autumn sowing on about 1.07 million hectares," he said.
Wheat is to be sown on 850,000 hectares this year, a significant increase over 582,965 ha in 1995.
The Commodity Reserve Agency will start selling the first 150 million dinar tranche of the new issue of contracts on the Belgrade bourse on October 3.
